name: WV-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Carol Miller seeking re-election with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Miller at roughly 98%
No public polling or expert ratings, but no evidence of a competitive race
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Miller: an R+22 district, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly seven-to-one over Democrat Vince George. Markets price her near certain, and nothing in the record suggests movement toward the challenger.
model.watch: Any late polling showing George within single digits, or a surge of outside spending against Miller, would be the first sign this is more than a safe Republican seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Carol Miller is seeking another term in a southern West Virginia district that leans Republican by more than twenty points. She has raised about $1.7 million and holds a wide cash advantage over Democrat Vince George, who has brought in roughly a quarter million with no outside help on either side. A Constitution Party candidate is also on the ballot.

Prediction markets give Miller about a 98% chance of winning, and no public polls or expert ratings flag the race as competitive. The forecast expects Miller to win by roughly nineteen points, consistent with the district's strong Republican lean and her incumbency advantage.
